chief_complaint: excruciating unilateral orbital pain with lacrimation
hpi_details: A 26-year-old female presents to the clinic with excruciating unilateral orbital pain with lacrimation. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: She thinks she might have a deep sinus infection or an impacted tooth root that is pressing into the back of her eye socket.
concerns: She is worried that the agonizing pain will permanently damage the nerves behind her eye and leave her blind.
expectations: She hopes to get an emergency eye scan and an immediate injection to stop the unbearable pain right now.

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Cluster Headache is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Cluster Headache: High-flow oxygen 100%, subcutaneous Sumatriptan, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

Key HPI features: A 26-year-old female presents to the clinic with excruciating unilateral orbital pain with lacrimation. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
Objective/Exam findings: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Cluster Headache.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Cluster Headache.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Migraine without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.

Ignoring critical warning signs such as: sudden 'thunderclap' onset reaching maximum intensity within seconds, new focal neurological deficits, papilloedema, reduced consciousness, or first presentation after age 50.
management_principles: Plan for Cluster Headache: High-flow oxygen 100%, subcutaneous Sumatriptan
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

Select appropriate diagnostic workup for Cluster Headache

teaching.one_liner: Excruciating unilateral orbital pain with tearing, often linked to alcohol and tobacco use, treated with high-flow oxygen.
red_flags: Sudden 'thunderclap' onset reaching maximum intensity within seconds — must exclude subarachnoid haemorrhage
New focal neurological deficits, papilloedema, or reduced consciousness — raises concern for a secondary cause rather than primary cluster headache
First presentation after age 50 — warrants imaging to exclude giant cell arteritis or a structural lesion

must_ask.say: Is the pain strictly around one eye?
Does your eye water or nose run during attacks?
Do you smoke or drink alcohol?
Does this happen at a similar time each day?
Do you feel like pacing during an attack?

history.answer: I have been having excruciating, unbearable pain around my right eye, and tears keep pouring down that side.
The attacks started about a week ago and have been getting worse. When an attack hits, the pain builds to a terrible peak within about five to ten minutes.
I get one or two attacks every day, and each episode usually lasts around forty-five minutes to an hour. I have never experienced anything like this before.
It is strictly on my right side, concentrated deep behind and around my right eye and spreading into my temple.
It feels like a sharp, hot poker stabbing directly through my eyeball. On a scale of one to ten, the pain is a definite ten.
The attacks usually strike at predictable times, especially waking me up from sound sleep around two in the morning.
I feel terribly restless and agitated whenever the pain starts. I cannot sit still or lie down, so I end up pacing back and forth across the room.
Lying down makes the throbbing feel much worse, while pacing around helps me endure it. Resting in a dark room does not make the pain go away.
During an attack, my right eye gets bloodshot and tears up heavily, my right eyelid droops slightly, and my right nostril gets stuffy and runny.
No, I don't see any flashing lights, zigzag lines, or blind spots before the headache begins.
I feel a bit nauseous simply because the pain is so agonizing, but I haven't thrown up. Bright lights and loud noises don't bother me the way they do in regular migraines.
No, I haven't had any fever, chills, or stiffness in my neck.
No, I haven't experienced any weakness in my arms or legs, numbness, slurred speech, confusion, or seizures.
My actual vision is clear, without any blurring or double vision, though it is hard to see while my eye is tearing up.
No, I haven't bumped my head or had any falls or injuries recently.
I tried taking regular over-the-counter pain relievers like ibuprofen and acetaminophen, but they didn't touch the pain at all.
I noticed that having even half a glass of wine triggered an intense attack within an hour. Lack of sleep also seems to make them happen more easily.
I don't have high blood pressure, and I do not take blood pressure medications or blood thinners.
No one else in my apartment has headaches or feels sick, and we don't use any unvented gas or fuel heaters.
No, I have never had cancer, HIV, or taken any immune-suppressing drugs.
I have been feeling drained and exhausted during the day because these nighttime attacks keep disrupting my sleep.
I thought maybe a severe sinus blockage or an infected tooth root was pressing straight behind my eyeball.

The pain is so unbearable that I'm terrified it is going to destroy my optic nerve and blind me in this eye. I just need an urgent scan of my eye socket and an injection right away to knock this agonizing pain out.
I have always been healthy and don't have any chronic medical conditions.
I have never had any surgeries and have never been hospitalized.
I don't take any daily prescription medications, over-the-counter drugs, or vitamin supplements.
I do not have any known allergies to medications, foods, or other substances.
No, I have never smoked cigarettes or used any tobacco products.
I am normally a light social drinker, but right now I am completely avoiding alcohol because it sets off the pain.
I work as an office administrator and live with my partner in an apartment.
My mother gets occasional mild tension headaches, but nobody in my family has ever had severe headaches like this.
My last period started two weeks ago, and my cycles are regular every twenty-eight days.
My partner and I use condoms consistently and correctly, and there is no possibility that I am pregnant.

exam.finding: Blood pressure is 124/82 mmHg, heart rate 78 beats per minute, respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute, body temperature 36.6°C, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Alert young female appearing tired and restless, pacing around the room, with mild residual conjunctival injection on the right side.
Pupils are equal, round, and reactive to light; extraocular movements are full, visual acuity is intact, and fundoscopy reveals sharp optic disc margins without papilledema.
No tenderness on palpation or percussion over the bilateral frontal and maxillary sinuses.
Neck is supple with full passive flexion, and both Kernig and Brudzinski signs are negative.
Cranial nerves II through XII are grossly intact with symmetric facial sensation and movement.
Normal muscle tone and bulk, with 5/5 motor strength throughout all four extremities.
Intact and symmetric sensation to light touch and pinprick across all extremities.
Deep tendon reflexes are 2+ and symmetric throughout, with down-going plantar responses bilaterally.
Normal finger-to-nose testing, rapid alternating movements, and steady tandem gait without ataxia.
